text: I will be home around seven o'clock, so we can have dinner together.
expect: Whisper returns it clean: skipped if the option is on.

text: I read through the minutes of Tuesday's meeting, and the only things missing are the list of attendees and the date of the next session.
expect: Clean too, and longer: this is where skipping the model saves the most.

text: Can you send me the quote before Friday noon?
expect: Read it as a question: it must stay a question.

text: Um, I think we could, uh, move the session to Thursday.
expect: Say the “um” and “uh”: if they stay in what Whisper heard, the model has to be called.

text: So, yeah, I will call you back tomorrow morning to talk about it.
The meeting is at ten o'clock, no sorry, at eleven o'clock.
expect: The pasted text must keep only eleven o'clock.

text: The meeting is at ten o'clock no at eleven o'clock.
expect: Read it in one go, without a pause: if it is skipped and “ten o'clock” stays, that is a wrong skip.

text: We leave on Monday, I mean Tuesday, depending on the weather.
expect: The pasted text must keep only Tuesday.

text: We leave on Monday I mean Tuesday depending on the weather.
expect: In one go: the pasted text must keep only Tuesday.

text: I, I wanted to tell you that the package has arrived.
I forwarded the invoice to Sarah Mitchell at Brightwater Logistics.
expect: Names are hard to hear: if they come out wrong, add them to the dictionary.

text: Why has the server stopped responding since this morning
expect: Read it without intonation: the “?” must appear.

text: You are sending me the quote before Friday
expect: Read it as a question: if it is skipped without a “?”, that is a wrong skip.

text: I added a skill in Claude Code to tidy the inbox of the Vault.
expect: “Claude Code” must be written like this: if it is not, add it to the dictionary (like your other words).

text: The invoice comes to one thousand two hundred and fifty dollars, to be paid before November fifteenth.
expect: Amount and date right, in digits or in words.

checks.label: amount right
forms: one thousand two hundred and fifty

text: You know, the thing is, we don't have time this week.
expect: Casual tone: “the thing” must stay. The model removes “you know” (a verbal tic); when skipped, the phrase keeps it.

text: For tomorrow's session, I suggest we start with five minutes of abdominal breathing, then a visualisation of the safe place, and finish with some time to share what everyone felt during the week.
expect: About twenty seconds: look mostly at the total time.
